summary: A broadleaf tree with a flared root collar, a four-segment leaning trunk, four branches and a crown of seven overlapping canopy lobes, with sway(dt) and an instancing handle for the lobe.
objective: At five metres the tree reads as a leaning trunk under a lobed crown, then branches reaching into their own lobes, then faceted shading, collars and hue jitter.
example_prompts: Plant a stand of trees behind the cottages.
I need a tree whose crown is not one green sphere.
not_for: Any claim about a botanical species, its growth habit or its wood.
Leaf-level foliage: the crown is seven lobes, not a leaf card system.

silhouette: a crown of seven overlapping lobes, never a single sphere
a trunk leaning about 5 degrees, with the lean growing up the tree
six root wedges splaying out of the base into the ground
medium: four branches reaching out to the lobes they carry
a bark collar over each of the three trunk segment joins
lobes of five different sizes, the crown lobe 15 percent larger than the rest
fine: flat-shaded facets across every lobe, so the crown catches light in planes
the trunk narrowing from 19 cm at the flare to 6 cm under the crown
per-lobe hue jitter of 10 percent across the seven lobes

principles: A crown of one sphere is the single tell of a procedural tree. Lobes cost nothing and they buy the whole silhouette.
A trunk that meets the ground as a clean cylinder reads as a dowel pushed into grass. The root flare is the cheapest fix.
The lobe tumble is baked into the geometry so an instance only spins about Y: a tilted instance inflates its axis-aligned box and lifts the framing off the tree.
implementation: Call create({ seed, age, lean, height, radius, leaf }); the group is centred on the trunk base with y = 0 at the ground.
animate(dt) - also exported as sway(dt) - rocks the crown and branches and returns true when it moved; it returns false for dt <= 0.
instancing gives { geometry, material, hueJitter }: hand them to THREE.InstancedMesh, or to kit-core scatterInstances with a hue per placement, to plant a wood from one draw call.
observable_checks: Run scripts/kit-proof.py and count features in close.png: at least two from each detail-ladder band must be visible.
age 0.4 and age 1.0 differ by more than 40 cm in crown height at the same seed.
animate(0) returns false and animate(0.4) returns true and moves the crown.

known_limits: Authored creative geometry. Nothing here measures a real tree, species or growth habit.
The poly budget is the triangle count observed at default parameters and stays inside the 2500 triangle ceiling this phase set for nature.
sway() rotates the crown group about its own origin, so at amplitudes above about 0.05 rad the lobes visibly slide off the branch tips.
Rotated lobe instances inflate the axis-aligned bounding box: the box is up to 20 percent wider than the crown actually is.

Palette values are the colours that render: kit-core scatterInstances runs its InstancedMesh on a white-based clone of the material and writes the absolute jittered colour per instance, so an unjittered instance lands on exactly the hex the parameter names.
creative_affordances: Any parameter may be pushed outside its stated range; the range is the band that was proved, not a limit.
Push lean past 0.3 and drop age for a wind-shaped coastal tree, or re-colour the leaf for autumn without touching the geometry.

defaults.rationale: A 3.2 m crown clears a cottage eave without hiding its roof, which is the one proportion that decides whether a tree frames a building or swallows it.
